findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "send_email" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "set_webhook" references sensitive artifacts (secret). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

evidence.snippet: Set (or clear with an empty url) the HTTPS webhook that receives call.completed, message.received, and email.received. Returns the signing secret once.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_line, book_reservation, get_call, list_messages, list_emails, get_email, get_settings, list_history · Private data: book_reservation, list_contacts, add_contact, remove_contact, set_webhook · Public sink: get_line, place_call, book_reservation, send_text, list_emails, get_email, send_email, forward_email, get_settings, set_bot_push, set_webhook, list_history · Destructive: remove_contact.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_line, book_reservation, get_call, list_messages, list_emails, get_email, get_settings, list_history · Private data: book_reservation, list_contacts, add_contact, remove_contact, set_webhook · Public sink: get_line, place_call, book_reservation, send_text, list_emails, get_email, send_email, forward_email, get_settings, set_bot_push, set_webhook, list_history · Destructive: remove_contact

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
